threads.body: [Javaagent] `JaxrsCodeAttributesGetter` is a stateless attributes getter, so retaining it as a singleton field conflicts with the repository convention and unnecessarily extends its lifetime. Keep it local to instrumenter registration, as the previous static initializer did.

replies.body:

The applicable Java style instructions prefer stateless attributes getters constructed at registration. Restored a static initializer with one local JaxrsCodeAttributesGetter shared by both extractors, removing the redundant field while preserving the finalized scope, controller enablement and instrumenter behavior. The complete JAX-RS module test suite passed.

threads.body: @copilot Please remove the `assertServiceScope()` teardown hooks from both `CxfJaxWs2Test` and `MetroJaxWs2Test`, but keep their scope-name coverage. In `AbstractJaxWs2Test`, add `.satisfies(hasScopeName(expectedScopeName()))` to the existing `HelloService/...` span assertions inside `waitAndAssertTraces(...)` for both successful and failing requests, using the shared `InstrumentationScopeAssertions.hasScopeName` helper. Have the concrete subclasses supply the expected scope through a protected `expectedScopeName()` hook: `io.opentelemetry.jaxws-2.0-cxf-3.0` for CXF and `io.opentelemetry.jaxws-2.0-metro-2.2` for Metro. Also update the existing Axis2 subclass for the shared hook, using its current scope `io.opentelemetry.jaxws-2.0-axis2-1.6`. Remove the unused teardown imports. This keeps the scope checks beside the existing trace assertions instead of separately filtering exported spans after every test.

replies.body: Updated in `ddb839ed`: scope checks now run within both shared success and failure trace assertions, with scope names supplied by the Axis2, CXF, and Metro subclasses.
